sourceEvidence.label: MSFS Landing Stats distribution and telemetry-ingress source evidence

assessment.summary: Two trust boundaries were hardened structurally: hostile telemetry ingestion is automatically enrolled, signed, strictly validated, and bounded by source/global/storage quotas; releases require a pinned signed manifest with the CI signing secret provisioned.

nonNegotiables: No shared private upload credential in the public executable.
assumptions: Client hosts are untrusted and cannot attest genuine simulator execution.
GitHub Actions can hold a repository signing secret.
Initial telemetry enrollment is automatic and creates no hardware fingerprint.

opportunities.title: Own the telemetry-ingress trust boundary
opportunities.summary: Bind each upload to an enrolled installation key and validate the complete archive before corpus admission.
opportunities.diagnosis: A public desktop client cannot protect a shared private credential or prove simulator provenance; the server must own admission, bounds, replay state, and revocation.

evidence.claim: A completed chunk is atomically closed before ChunkCompleted is raised.
A signed synthetic capture traversed the public tunnel, passed validation, received an ACK, and was removed from the test corpus.
A common private key shipped in the EXE would be extractable and would authorize arbitrary forged captures.

desiredInvariants: Every accepted capture is bound to an active installation key, fresh nonce, signed size, and signed SHA-256.
Untrusted ZIP content is bounded and fully validated before corpus admission.
The server can revoke one installation without rotating every client.
A failed upload leaves the completed local capture intact and never disables DEBUG RAW or blocks SimConnect.
Public enrollment has a global request budget, atomic registry cap, stale-unreferenced retention, and free-space gate.

options.title: Shared credential in the executable
options.summary: Gate requests with one embedded signing secret.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Extraction of one client credential grants global authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: One extracted key defeats admission for every installation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt static and runtime extraction from a release binary.

tradeoffs.assessment: One signature adds negligible work relative to upload.
Only bounded key material is retained.
Simple validation does not improve queue recovery.
Any leak requires a fleet-wide credential and client rotation.
It is initially easy to deploy.

residualRisks: A copied credential authorizes unlimited identities and forged telemetry.

options.title: Per-install keys with automatic enrollment
options.summary: Generate a DPAPI-protected key per installation and let the server own enrollment, replay, source/global quota, validation, and revocation.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The existing completion event is a safe queue boundary.
The complete public path was exercised.
Compromise is limited to one revocable installation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-install authority, nonce replay protection, strict ZIP validation, source/global budgets, storage ceiling, and free-space reserve bound abuse.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Repeat signature, replay, source/global quota, storage reserve, and malformed archive tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: One-sample public E2E completed interactively; large-file throughput remains unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Upload 1, 8, and 16 MB captures and require no SimConnect-thread work.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming caps client and server buffers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS during a 16 MB upload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closed ZIPs form a retryable bounded queue and are deleted only after ACK.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Interrupt network and process across upload stages.

tradeoffs.assessment: Revocation, enrollment/registry budgets, SQLite, retention, and tunnel health require ownership.
Only newly enabled DEBUG RAW sessions enter the queue.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify old local archives are not auto-enqueued.

residualRisks: An enrolled hostile client can still fabricate syntactically valid telemetry.
Distributed clients can consume the bounded global enrollment and capture budgets, causing temporary fail-closed rejection.

workPackages: Monitor enrollment, source/global budgets, storage and rejects.
acceptanceCriteria: Automatic signed public E2E succeeds and malformed/replayed/quota-exceeding requests fail.
migrationNotes: First use requires explicit telemetry consent; enrollment is automatic.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable DEBUG RAW upload and stop the isolated Compose project; queued ZIPs remain recoverable.

opportunities.recommendation: Use automatic per-install key enrollment with explicit consent. Treat corpus provenance as untrusted and enforce source/global byte budgets plus hard storage and free-space ceilings.

opportunities.title: Authenticate self-updates independently of transport
opportunities.summary: Require a signed canonical two-asset manifest and an independently verifying updater before replacing application files.
opportunities.diagnosis: HTTPS and a hash served from the same compromised release account do not provide an independent authenticity decision.

evidence.claim: The standalone updater re-verifies the signed versioned manifest, its own hash, the package, target identity, archive topology, and assembly version before transactional replacement.
The workflow publishes a portable ZIP and updater bound by one signed format-2 manifest.

desiredInvariants: No downloaded helper or package is trusted without a signature from the pinned release key.
Signed sizes and SHA-256 values bind both exact assets.
The updater confirms the requesting PID and path before shutdown.
Partial multi-file replacement rolls back to the previous application.

options.title: HTTPS plus release hash
options.summary: Trust GitHub transport and a colocated SHA-256.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Detects transfer damage but not a compromised publisher.

tradeoffs.assessment: Detects accidental corruption only.
One SHA-256 pass is required.
Streaming hash is bounded.
Corrupt assets are rejected.
No signing key operations are needed.
Minimal workflow change.

residualRisks: A GitHub publisher compromise can replace both asset and hash.

options.title: Pinned signed release manifest
options.summary: Sign a canonical manifest in CI and verify it with a pinned public key before download installation.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The verified standalone helper owns replacement after an identity handshake.
The workflow signs both stable release assets together.

tradeoffs.assessment: GitHub asset substitution is rejected without the separate signing key.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Serve a modified manifest and asset.

tradeoffs.assessment: Startup adds small metadata requests; asset download happens only for a newer version.
Manifest and file hashing are bounded.
Exact archive validation, identity handshake, transaction backup, and reverse rollback reduce partial-update failure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Interrupt each replacement phase and verify restoration.

tradeoffs.assessment: The signing secret needs backup, access control, and rotation procedure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a key-loss and rotation tabletop.

tradeoffs.assessment: v0.7.0 needs one manual ZIP bootstrap because its removed format-1 SFX client cannot consume format 2.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Upgrade from v0.7.1 to the next signed format-2 build.

residualRisks: A compromise of both GitHub publishing authority and the release signing key remains fatal.
There is no automatic rollback after a semantically broken but correctly signed release.

acceptanceCriteria: Both EXEs scan clean; signed update restarts; manifest, helper, package, topology, identity, and version tampering are rejected; partial replacement rolls back.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Preserve the transaction backup, remove the faulty release from latest, and publish a corrected higher version.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the signed two-asset manifest and standalone verified helper; add Authenticode later for reputation, while retaining the independent pinned-key decision.

openQuestions: Where will the offline backup of the release private key be kept?
What retention/privacy text will be shown outside the one-time consent dialog?
